newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean panel mulls mergers of financial firms.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean panel mulls mergers of financial firms.

text.p: A presidential financial reform panel is considering a plan to encourge mergers and acquisitions among troubled financial institutions in South Korea, a commission statement said on Friday.
The Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said the plan would improve the efficiency of financial institutions.
The statement said the commission would draft legislation enabling an authority to demand that stricken financial firms come up with a rescue plan or merge with other institutions.
If targetted financial institutions failed to meet these requirements, the authority would have the right to cancel their licence, the commission statement said.
Banks would be classified into five or six categories in accordance with the capital adequacy ratio set by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), it said.
The BIS recommends a capital adequacy ratio of at least eight percent. Banks whose ratio dropped below eight percent banks would have to increase their capital.
The commission said it would consider extending tax benefits and financial aid to merged financial institutions.
The presidential panel also said it was discussing ways to stabilise Korea's relatively high interest rates.
It said it would propose reforms to control and manage money supply and further liberalise the domestic capital market.
The 31-member commission was set up in January after President Kim Young-sam said he would push forward with reforming the financial sector.
The commission is expected to present its proposals by the end of May. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
